headline: The database and RLS hold under every attack tried, and run 1's five Majors are fixed. One new Major: when the code email fails to send, the API still answers success and the screen says a code is on its way. A second: run 1's web-side fixes are pinned only by QA's own specs, which no CI job runs. Six Minors, four of them on screens (a live-session suspension says nothing, Undo on You doesn't redraw, You errors offline in a browser, a long email is clipped).

suites.diff: 1 screen changed (settings/account, as the brief asks), 0 new, 1 unexplored (reading, unchanged), 0 check findings

findings.title: When the code email fails to send, the API answers 200 "success" and the screen says a code was sent
findings.detail: Better Auth runs `sendVerificationOTP` through `runInBackgroundOrAwait`, which catches and logs any error (`better-auth/dist/context/create-context.mjs:215`). So a Gmail failure (a wrong or revoked app password, Gmail's daily limit, an outage) answers `200 {"success":true}`; sign-in moves to *Type the code* and says *Sen sent a 6-digit code to …*, and nothing ever arrives. Only Vercel's function log knows. With an unreachable SMTP host the request also hangs for nodemailer's 2-minute connect timeout before answering 200. Nothing in `api.test.ts` drives a failing mailer: its mailer always succeeds. This bites the owner's first production sign-in and makes Q14 (*inbox or spam?*) unanswerable when the real answer is *never sent*. patterns.md §7 *Error*: say what happened and what to do next.

findings.title: Run 1's web-side fixes are pinned only by QA's own specs, which nothing in CI runs
findings.detail: Phase-3 probe: in `apps/web/src/data/auth.ts` `signedOut()` was made to read *can't ask the server* as signed out again (run 1's Major 3, a signed-in person opening Sen offline lands on sign-in). `pnpm test` stayed 320/320 and `pnpm --filter @sen/web e2e:server` stayed 1/1: `e2e/server.spec.ts` only walks sign-in online, and `pnpm e2e` builds with the fake backend, where the gate is skipped. Only QA's `qa/e2e/b05-offline.spec.ts` (FLOW-10c) and this run's FLOW-23 went red, and no workflow runs `qa/e2e`. The same holds for the sign-in screen's mapping of a 429 to *wait a minute* (run 1's 4) and the *paused* message (run 1's 10): their API halves are in `api.test.ts`, their screen halves only in `qa/e2e`. The ledger cites QA's specs as the evidence, so the fixes were real, but nothing will say when they regress. Move FLOW-10c (and the paused and wait messages) into `apps/web/e2e/server.spec.ts`, which CI's `db` job runs.

findings.title: Undo on Settings → You restores the server, but the screen keeps showing the undone value
findings.detail: Set the payday to day 12, tap the toast's *Undo*: `user_settings.expected_payday` is back to `last-working` with a second audit row, but the screen still has *A day* ticked with 12 in the field, because `you.tsx` keeps the payday in `useState` initialised once from the query. A reload shows the truth. A person reads the wrong payday until then, and editing the day again would write it back. Not checked whether `main`'s fake backend shows the same (the screen is B04's), but B05 is what makes the undo real.

findings.title: A write and its retry sent at the same moment are both audited
findings.detail: `setYou` reads the row, compares, then upserts, under READ COMMITTED with no lock, so two identical requests in flight both see the old value and both write an audit row (the second with a stale *before*). The state ends right; the audit log gets a duplicate, and each has its own *Undo*. A `SELECT … FOR UPDATE` on the person's row (or an upsert with `WHERE … IS DISTINCT FROM`) would close it. An outbox retry after a timeout is exactly this case.

findings.title: In a browser, going offline on Settings → You replaces the loaded payday with *Couldn't load your details*
findings.detail: Signed in on the preview build, You loaded, then `context.setOffline(true)`: within 2 s the screen became the error state, while the banner above it promises *What you add is kept and syncs when you're back*. flows.md `offline`: in a browser, offline is read-only, so what was loaded should stay readable, and the banner's promise isn't true of a browser's writes (§5: in a browser, writes go straight to the API, online only). Settings → You is the only server-backed screen in B05, so it's the first to show this; every slice that moves a screen to the server will inherit it.

findings.title: The API's own routes check neither Origin nor Content-Type; SameSite=Lax is the only cross-site guard
findings.detail: Better Auth's routes refuse a foreign Origin (`INVALID_ORIGIN`), but `/api/commands` accepts one, and accepts a `text/plain` body. Browsers don't send a `SameSite=Lax` cookie on a cross-site POST, so no page can use this today; it's one setting away from mattering (a `SameSite=None` change for the shell, say).

findings.title: docs/local.md's Q14 SQL inserts the test address as typed
findings.detail: `auth_sign_in_check` compares `auth_user.email` with `lower(trim(address))`, and the seed lower-cases, but the hand-run `insert into auth_user … values ('Test', 'you@outlook.com', true)` doesn't. An address typed with a capital (common on a phone keyboard) would then be *Sen is invitation-only*. `lower('…')` in the step fixes it.
